title: Vendor Handoff & Customer Runbook Template for Private Installations (V1.0)
author: Diego Campos
body:
Summary
This page is a vendor handoff and customer-facing runbook template intended for Redwood Inference private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It codifies the minimal set of artifacts, operational procedures, and contact/ownership assignments that must be delivered at project close. Use this as a canonical source when transitioning from delivery to customer-run steady state or Aruba/partner-managed operations.

Goals
- Provide a predictable, auditable handoff that reduces mean time to independent operations.
- Ensure customers have the runbooks, checks, and rollback actions necessary to meet initial SLOs.
- Standardize the artifact set and format to speed audits and compliance reviews.

Audience
- Customer engineering and SRE teams receiving a Private deployment.
- Redwood delivery engineers and customer success managers (CSMs).
- Third-party integrators and channel partners performing day-2 activities.

What to deliver (artifact checklist)
1) Deployment summary (high-level)
   - Model(s) hosted and pinned versions
   - Topology diagram (control plane, data plane, NAT/VPN, subnets)
   - Resource inventory (GPU types, NICs, storage classes)
2) Access and secrets
   - Admin user list and least-privilege roles
   - KMS/HSM integration notes and key IDs
   - SSH jump host and bastion procedures
3) Observability and alerts
   - Metrics dashboard URLs, retention, and RBAC
   - Alert runbook links and threshold definitions (CPU/GPU util, token latency, error rate)
4) Day-2 runbook (see sections below)
5) Upgrade and rollback playbook (brief and pointers to full ADR)
6) Compliance evidence pointers (audits, SBOM, signed images)
7) Contact matrix and escalation paths

Runbook: Day-2 Quick Reference (one-page)
- Owner: Customer SRE (primary), Redwood Oncall (secondary)
- Core SLOs: 99.5% availability for inference gateway; p95 generation latency < 350ms for 1k-token requests in baseline tests
- Service names: inference-gateway, kvcache-service, model-loader, batch-coordinator

Typical operational checks (daily)
- Health: systemctl status inference-gateway; docker ps | grep model-loader
- Metrics: ensure GPU memory pressure < 85%; queue length < 20 requests/worker
- Logs: tail /var/log/redwood/inference-gateway.log for ERROR or OOM

Escalation matrix (contact order)
1) Customer primary SRE on-call: listed in customer contact sheet
2) Redwood CSM: csm@redwood.ai (for business/contract issues)
3) Redwood delivery engineer (named in Handoff Summary)
4) Redwood Engineering on-call: redwood-ops pager (critical production P1s)

Acceptance checklist (minimum)
| Item | Owner | Pass criteria | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Basic network connectivity | Delivery | VPC peering or VPN established; test IPs reachable | ping, traceroute outputs attached |
| Model load test | Delivery + Customer | 500 concurrent small requests with < 300ms p95 | load test report (k6/hey) |
| Latency baseline | Delivery | p50/p95 latency under contractual baseline | grafana dashboard link |
| RBAC and secrets | Customer | All admin keys rotated; KMS access verified | KMS audit logs |
| Observability wired | Delivery | Metrics and logs appear in customer workspace with retention | screenshots and runbook links |

Minimum commands & snippets
- Check model process: sudo systemctl status redwood-model-loader
- Dump recent error logs: journalctl -u redwood-model-loader -n 500 --no-pager > /tmp/model-loader-errors.log
- Validate KV cache warm: curl -sS http://localhost:18081/kvcache/metrics | grep warm_cache_hits

Rollback & mitigation triggers (short)
- Trigger: model load failures > 5% for 10 minutes => Action: immediate route to previous model tag (see rollback steps)
- Trigger: p95 latency > 2x baseline for 15m => Action: enable degraded-mode routing (route new traffic to lower-capacity instance group) and open incident

Rollback steps (safe quick path)
1) Notify stakeholders and set incidents state to P1
2) Switch traffic via router-policy to the previous model tag: api call to control-plane /v1/routing/switch 
   Example: curl -X POST https://controlplane.example/api/v1/routing/switch -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"service":"inference-gateway","target_tag":"model-v1.3.2"}'
3) Monitor p95 and error rate for 10 minutes; if stable close incident and schedule root cause analysis
4) If rollback fails, scale up burst-capacity pool and engage Redwood on-call

Detailed handoff steps (delivery engineer)
1) Pre-handoff dry run with customer SRE (recommended 2 weeks before final cutover). Record all deviations.
2) Freeze configuration: tag Terraform; export runtime manifests and signed container image digests.
3) Execute smoke test suite jointly; capture artifacts and upload to shared bucket.
4) Walk customer through runbook and perform a live failover simulation (canary -> baseline -> rollback).
5) Provide final handoff packet (zipped): topology.pdf, runbook.md, acceptance_report.pdf, contacts.csv, signed-images.json, SBOM.json

Operational maturity levels (adoption guidance)
- Level 1 (Redwood-managed): Redwood maintains day-2, handoff is informational.
- Level 2 (Partner-assisted): Partner performs day-2; customer has read-only access and runbooks.
- Level 3 (Customer-operated): Customer owns full operations using this runbook as the canonical source.

Handoff email template (copy into ticket)
Subject: Redwood Private Deployment Handoff — <customer-name> — <env>
Body:
Team,
Attached is the handoff packet for <customer-name> <env>. Delivery summary: models pinned to tags, control plane endpoint, initial SLAs. Please confirm receipt and primary on-call.
Attachments: topology.pdf, runbook.md, acceptance_report.pdf, contacts.csv

Key contacts:
- Delivery lead: Diego Campos, diego@redwood.ai
- Redwood on-call: redwood-ops@pager.company (see runbook for routing)
- Customer SRE primary: ______________________ (fill before handoff)

Related artifacts and references
- Private delivery contract and operational contract page (link included in related_pages)
- Upgrade/rollback ADR (linked in customer handoff packet)

Notes and best practices
- Rotate keys immediately after handoff and validate KMS audit logs.
- Run a scheduled smoke test every 24 hours for the first 30 days.
- Capture token-level cost for the first 14 days to validate billing and autoscaling heuristics.

Revision history
- V1.0 2025-09-10: Initial published template
- V1.1 2026-01-12: Added rollback quick commands and SLO baseline examples
